Maladaptive Strategies.value: I throw myself into work or tasks to keep my mind occupied
go over and over why the event happened to me
work excessively to avoid being alone with thoughts

Threat.value: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked

Memory.value: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.
My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things

Negative Appraisals.value: I should have protected others and I failed
Somebody else would not have gotten into this situation
I am not sure my life is worth living anymore

vignette: Sarah, a 40-year-old European-American data scientist married to her high school sweetheart, has been struggling with the aftermath of witnessing a traumatic event that occurred during a work trip to an Arab village. She had been visiting for a project and one evening witnessed a severe altercation between locals and military personnel, which culminated in a fire breaking out, causing significant distress and trauma. The memory of the fire and flames is particularly potent for Sarah; any exposure to similar visual triggers can instantly bring back the full intensity of that event. For instance, she had recently started working on a project involving data visualization with flame-like graphics, and every time she encountered these visuals, she would suddenly feel as if the traumatic experience were happening again. This has made her work environment increasingly stressful, often leaving her feeling overwhelmed and anxious. Sarah's husband noticed that since the incident, she has been throwing herself into her work more than usual. She explained that keeping herself busy was one of the ways she coped with the trauma, allowing her to avoid being alone with her thoughts. Overworking became a way for Sarah to manage her emotional turmoil, but it also led to increased stress and fatigue, creating a vicious cycle where the stress from overwork itself triggered more intrusive memories. One day, while walking home from work, she saw an advertisement that showed flames in the background, and this immediately transported her back to that terrifying night. She vividly heard the sounds of shouting and sirens again, which felt so real and intense that it reinforced her belief that her life was not worth living anymore. This experience intensified her negative appraisals, particularly the feeling that she failed to protect others and should have done more. Sarah’s negative self-appraisals have made her hyper-vigilant about potential threats. Simple activities like walking home from work or checking doors and windows multiple times each night have become routine because she feels threatened by strangers even in ordinary situations. This heightened sense of threat has also fueled her overworking, as she believes that staying occupied with tasks can somehow shield her from further psychological harm. The memories are more real than normal, often intruding without warning when she least expects it. Sarah frequently goes over and over why the event happened to her, ruminating on whether she could have done something differently. This rumination often leads her back into the cycle of negative appraisals, reinforcing her belief that someone else would not have gotten into this situation. Sarah’s relationship with her husband has also been affected. She avoids discussing the incident and keeps herself isolated at home, further exacerbating her feelings of isolation and worthlessness. Her husband is concerned about her constant overworking and avoidance behaviors but struggles to understand how deeply she is suffering. The stress from these experiences culminated in a recent argument with her husband when she broke down during dinner after seeing a news report involving an altercation similar to the one she witnessed. This was the final straw for Sarah, who realized that she needed help navigating through this trauma. She is most afraid of never feeling safe or normal again but also hopes to regain some semblance of peace and control over her life. Sarah’s journey towards seeking therapy marks a critical step in addressing her symptoms and working towards recovery.
